content.title: Masters 2026 TV and streaming schedule offers viewers numerous options
content.text: Got 136 hours to spare?If you're a golf fan and wait for Masters week like a kid at Christmas, that's how much time you could invest from April 9-12 in live TV and streaming coverage of competition in the 90th Masters Tournament at the Augusta National Golf Club in Augusta, Ga.AdvertisementIt's part of an overall package of live and streaming coverage of the Masters that involves, for the first time, Prime Video April 9-10. The Prime coverage, from 1-3 p.m. each day, will lead into ESPN's coverage of the first two rounds, while Paramount+ will provide weekend streaming coverage from 12-2 p.m. that leads into the CBS coverage.Rory McIlroy celebrates his 2025 Masters championship at the Augusta National Golf Club.There will also be live streaming coverage of action on three areas of the golf course, Nos. 4-6, Nos. 11-13 (Amen Corner) and Nos. 15-16, plus feature groups.The live coverage on ESPN and CBS (counting two hours of the Par 3 Contest on ESPN April 8) totals 28 hours. The streaming coverage of hole Nos. 4-6, 11-13 and 15-16, plus feature groups, adds another 108 hours.AdvertisementThe amount of coverage available to viewers is a departure from a piece of Masters history, in which late Augusta National Golf Club chairman Clifford Roberts believed less was more and allowed TV cameras only on the second nine. It was 2000 before first-nine coverage was allowed."The Masters lives 365 [days]," lead CBS analyst Jim Nantz said on a March 30 teleconference. "People talk about it all year long. It's an amazing undertaking with what we're doing with all of these sources. I don't know where it goes next but I'm blown away by the amount of venues we have to present the Masters."Nantz will be working his 41st Masters, which began in 1986 when he was the 16th hole reporter when Jack Nicklaus won his record sixth green jacket. He will be joined by Trevor Immelman, with Dottie Pepper, Frank Nobilo, Andrew Catalon, Colt Knost and Amanda Balonis as on-course reporters.Masters fans can watch from practice to final puttFor fans who really want to immerse themselves:Advertisement"On The Range," will provide two hours each day, beginning with practice rounds on April 7, of Masters contestants hitting balls at the practice area, with live and recorded data on every single shot from each player during their range sessions. (Announcers will be Balonis, Kelly Tighlman, Michael Breed, Brian Crowell and Ioan Stephen).New for 2026 is "Inside Amen Corner," a dedicated feed on Prime Video that will offer a stats-enhanced viewing experience and feature an in-depth look into the strategy behind Hole Nos. 11, 12 and 13. The feature will stream from approximately 10:45 a.m.-6 p.m. for the first two rounds and 11:45 a.m.-6 p.m for the weekend rounds. (Announcers will be Grant Boone and Mark Immelman).SiriusXM will also broadcast live from 2-7:30 p.m. in the first two rounds and 2-7 p.m. on the weekend. ESPN Deportes will air live coverage of the first and second rounds for Spanish-speaking U.S. viewers from 3-7 p.m. in the first two rounds, 5-6 p.m. in the third round and 5-7 p.m. in the final round.All live coverage will be available on Masters.com and the Masters App, including the TV broadcast, featured groups, Hole Nos. 4, 5 and 6 (past PGA Tour winners Jeff Sluman and Scott Verplank, plus Dave Fleming and Matt Barrie), Amen Corner, Inside Amen Corner, Hole Nos. 15 and 16 (Stephen, Geoff Ogilvy, Ned Michaels) and On the Range.Ponte Vedra Beach resident and five-time PGA Tour winner Billy Kratzert will be involved in the Feature Group coverage along with another past Tour winner, Johnson Wagner, Breed and Crowell.The Masters will provide extensive coverage of action at the Augusta National Golf Club's "Amen Corner," hole Nos. 11, 12 and 13.Golf Channel, ESPN studio coverageThere will be no shortage of analysis pre- and post-round. Golf Channel's "Live From the Masters" will begin on April 7 from 2-5 p.m. and will air for a total of 52 hours. ESPN's "SportsCenter at the Masters" will be on April 8-10 for a total of 8 hours, 30 minutes and "Mornings at the Masters," returns April 8-12 on Masters YouTube.Masters fans can access 'Every Shot, Every Hole'In addition to live coverage, Masters digital platforms will offer scoring, interactive player tracking, video highlights and features and in-depth tournament news.AdvertisementMasters.com and the Masters App will continue to offer "Every Shot, Every Hole," along with "My Group," which serves as a personalized featured group for all 20,000+ videos.New for 2026, "Masters Vault Search" enables fans to explore and watch tournament clips spanning more than 50 years of Masters final round broadcasts through simple, conversation-style prompts. Additionally, player pages now feature Every Shot, Every Hole historical video dating back to 2019.Masters week TV/Streaming coverageMonday, April 6 On the Range, 12-2 p.m. (CBS Sports Digital, CBS
